title: Peak-free words vs. images of morphological dilation/erosion (Hardin array families)
claim: Theorem 1: for every k>=1 and n>=1, the number of words x(0..n+1) over {0..k} with no interior element strictly greater than both neighbours equals the number of words of length n+3 over {0..k} in which every nonzero entry is <= some neighbour (the 'n X 1 arrays with every nonzero element less than or equal to some horizontal or vertical neighbor' family). Bijection: 2-window max-filter (dilation) with 0-padding composed with complement, inverse = 2-window min-filter (erosion). Theorem 2: words of length n+2 over {0..k} with no strict interior peak and no strict interior valley are equinumerous with images of the 3-window min-filter on words of length n+3 (the 'n X 1 arrays of the minimum value of corresponding elements and their horizontal and vertical (and diagonal) neighbours' family); bijection via 2-window max, inverse 2-window min padded with top value k.
notes: Two independent triage agents found these. Also identify EVERY other OEIS pair resolved by these theorems: search the local OEIS data (/tmp/claude-0/oeis/stripped.gz and names.gz, and the full entries via the git repo at /tmp/claude-0/oeis/oeisdata, where `git -C /tmp/claude-0/oeis/oeisdata show HEAD:seq/A200/A200881.seq` prints any entry) for the whole Hardin families (other k, table versions like 'n X k' tables whose column 1 is involved), and list which members are not cross-referenced yet. Check whether the identities also hold for the full Hardin tables (not only the 1-column versions).

title: Kimberling's harmonic-number greedy sequence A228016 equals the hex-triangular indices A087125
claim: A228016 (a(1)= least k with 1/1+...+1/5 < H(k)-H(5); a(n) = least k with H(a(n-1))-H(5) < H(k)-H(a(n-1)) ... read the exact definition in the entry) coincides with A087125 (indices k of hex numbers 3k(k+1)+1 that are triangular), shifted by one. Consequence: A228016's recurrence a(n)=11a(n-1)-11a(n-2)+a(n-3) and its g.f., both marked 'conjectured' in the entry (Kimberling 2013), become theorems.
notes: Triage sketch: with b=a+1/2, b_n=10b_{n-1}-b_{n-2}, b_n b_{n-2} - b_{n-1}^2 = -3; H(m)=ln(m+1/2)+gamma+1/(24(m+1/2)^2)+O(m^-4) gives a greedy threshold b_n - (r^2/24-3)/b_{n-2} with r=5+2sqrt6, margin ~1.08>0. A rigorous proof needs EXPLICIT two-sided error bounds for H(m) - ln(m+1/2) - gamma (e.g. from the Euler-Maclaurin remainder, or known inequalities such as DeTemple's) valid for all m beyond some small m0, plus direct computation below m0. Verified numerically for n<=88 with 400-digit arithmetic.

title: A112051 = (prime(n)^2-1)/2 (A216244) via least quadratic non-residues
claim: A112051 records first indices where A112046 takes a new value. Triage argument: A112046 values are primes; prime p first appears at index (p^2-1)/2 unless a prime r in (p^2-p, p^2) has least quadratic non-residue n(r) exactly p; this reduces to showing n(r) < sqrt(r)-1 for all relevant primes r (exception r=23 for p=5 is harmless). Needs explicit bounds on the least quadratic non-residue (e.g. classical n(p) < sqrt(p) bounds such as Vinogradov/elementary n(p) <= (1+sqrt(4p-3))/2 type, or Treviño's explicit Burgess bounds) together with computation for small p.
notes: Read A112046's exact definition first and re-derive the reduction carefully; the elementary bound n(p)(n(p)-1) < p might already be sufficient or nearly so. Make the proof complete and explicit, including all small cases by computation.

title: Closed form for four-cuboid tilings of the n x n x n cube (A386884, 2025)
claim: The number of distinct four-cuboid combinations filling an n X n X n cube using only strict cuboids (read the exact definition in A386884, including what 'strict' and 'distinct combination' mean) equals (n-4)*T(ceil((n-4)/2)) where T(m)=m(m+1)/2, for all n (check the offset/small n).
notes: Triage proof sketch: every tiling of a box by 4 boxes is guillotine (corner-counting), strict pieces force two n x n x t slabs each cut once; count distinct multisets {{s,t},{n-s,t},{s',n-t},{n-s',n-t}}; brute force for n<=9, formula checked to n=89. Write a complete rigorous proof, including the guillotine lemma for 4 boxes in 3D (be careful: it is false for 5 boxes in 2D - pinwheel - so the argument must use the count 4).

title: A225034 (101-avoiding binary words) = inverse binomial transform of A048775, and Berselli's conjectured recurrence
claim: A225034(n) = A005773(n)+A005773(n+1) = inverse binomial transform of C(2n+3,n+1); hence A163765 = A225034 (n>=3). Also check whether this proves the recurrence (n+1)a(n)-(2n+3)a(n-1)-3(n-2)a(n-2)=0 that the A225034 entry labels 'Conjecture' (Berselli 2013), or whether that recurrence is already a consequence of a proven g.f. in the entry.
notes: Give a self-contained proof (generating functions are fine) and say precisely what is new relative to the entries.

title: Eventual closed form of Hardin's table A253435
claim: For the table T(n,k) of (n+1)X(k+1) 0..1 arrays with every 2X2 subblock diagonal minus antidiagonal sum nondecreasing horizontally and vertically (read exact definition), T(n,k) = 9*2^(n-1) + 9*2^(k-1) + 12 for all n,k >= 4, even though the rule is not transpose-symmetric and the table is asymmetric for small n.
notes: Give a structural proof valid for ALL n,k>=4 simultaneously (a classification of valid arrays), not only per-column transfer matrices. Compute the table independently to confirm.

title: R. J. Mathar's June 2025 conjectures A282297 = A279721 and A282295 = A279720 (n>=2)
claim: Test the conjectures stated in those entries (both by R. J. Mathar, Jun 21 2025): rule-451 x-axis readouts equal rule-193 readouts for n>=2. Triage simulations found that rule 449 and rule 451 readouts differ at n=26 and rule 193 vs 449 differ at n=30, which does not directly settle 451 vs 193.
notes: Implement the 2D von Neumann 5-cell outer-totalistic... careful: these are Wolfram-numbered 2D CA rules on the 5-cell von Neumann neighborhood as used in Robert Price's OEIS entries (read the Mathematica programs in the entries and reproduce ALL stored terms of A279720, A279721, A282295, A282297 before trusting the simulator).
